drivingQuestion: From where do we know the final betrothed nullifies vows disclosed to the first betrothed?
outcomeNote: Shmuel's derivation stands via the superfluous word עליה

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ מְנָלַן דְּאָרוּס אַחֲרוֹן מֵיפֵר נְדָרִים שֶׁנִּרְאוּ לְאָרוּס רִאשׁוֹן? אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל, אָמַר קְרָא: ״וְאִם הָיוֹ תִהְיֶה לְאִישׁ וּנְדָרֶיהָ עָלֶיהָ״. נְדָרִים שֶׁהָיוּ עָלֶיהָ כְּבָר. דִּלְמָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי שֶׁלֹּא נִרְאוּ לְאָרוּס רִאשׁוֹן, אֲבָל נְדָרִים שֶׁנִּרְאוּ לְאָרוּס רִאשׁוֹן — לָא מָצֵי מֵיפַר אָרוּס אַחֲרוֹן!
segments.en: «GEMARA:» «From where do we» derive «that» her «final betrothed can nullify» her «vows that were disclosed to the first betrothed? Shmuel said» that «the verse states: “And if she be to a husband and her vows are upon» her…and he nullifies her vow” (Numbers 30:7–9), indicating that he can nullify «vows that were upon her already.» The Gemara asks: «Perhaps this statement applies» only to vows «that were not discerned by the first betrothed, but vows that were discerned by the first betrothed,» the «final betrothed cannot nullify.»

The Gemara answers: The phrase «“upon her” is a superfluous» part of the «verse.» One can derive from it that all her vows, including those of which an earlier betrothed had been aware, can be nullified by the final betrothed.
